title: Wanderers to Host 2027 World Cup Final and India–Pakistan Clash
excerpt: The ICC has released the 2027 men's ODI World Cup schedule, with Johannesburg's Wanderers hosting both the India–Pakistan clash on October 10 and the final on November 21, and an official ticket ballot now open.
body:
• The ICC has released the 2027 men's ODI World Cup schedule: the final will be played at the Wanderers in Johannesburg on November 21, 2027, with a reserve day on November 22.
  • The same venue, the 'Bullring', hosts the India vs Pakistan group-stage clash on October 10 — three days after India opens its campaign against defending champions Australia at Newlands, Cape Town.
  • The 14-team tournament, co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, runs across 12 venues, with a new Super 7 second round replacing the old Super 12-style format.
  • The ICC opened an official ticket ballot on October 1, running until November 21, with entry-level tickets priced from about USD 9.62.

The International Cricket Council has unveiled the schedule for the 2027 men's ODI World Cup, and it carries a double dose of marquee cricket for one ground: Johannesburg's Wanderers Stadium will host both the India vs Pakistan group match on October 10, 2027, and the tournament final on November 21.

The 14-team event, co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, will begin with a pre-tournament Super Series in Windhoek on October 2, with the group stage opening on October 7. India, led by Shubman Gill, begins its campaign against defending champions Australia at Newlands in Cape Town — an immediate rematch of the 2023 final, which Australia won in Ahmedabad.

Three days later comes the fixture the whole subcontinent circles: India vs Pakistan at the Wanderers, the high-scoring ground nicknamed the 'Bullring' that also stages the final, according to Reuters. India's group itinerary then takes them to Centurion for Afghanistan on October 14, Bloemfontein for Qualifier A on October 17, and the newly constructed Victoria Falls Stadium for co-hosts Zimbabwe on October 24.

Context & Background

The schedule release, announced on October 1, locks in a new tournament structure. Twelve teams qualify directly for the group stage — hosts South Africa and Zimbabwe, plus the best eight sides on the ICC men's ODI rankings at the September 30, 2026 cut-off — with the remaining four spots decided at the Cricket World Cup Qualifier. The West Indies were not among the direct qualifiers and must come through the qualifying route.

The confirmed groups: Group A features India, Australia, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Zimbabwe and one qualifier; Group B has South Africa, England, New Zealand, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and another qualifier. The top three from each pool, plus the better fourth-place finisher across the two groups, advance to a new 'Super 7' round — a seven-team round-robin played with no carryover points — from which the top four reach the semi-finals in Cape Town (November 17) and Centurion (November 18), both with reserve days.

Twelve venues across three countries will host matches: eight in South Africa (Cape Town, Paarl, Johannesburg, Tshwane, Bloemfontein, Durban, East London and Gqeberha), three in Zimbabwe (Harare, Bulawayo and the new Mosi-oa-Tunya Stadium at Victoria Falls) and one in Namibia, where Windhoek hosts the Super Series and three group games.

Impact & Analysis

Putting the final and the India–Pakistan fixture at the same venue concentrates the tournament's two biggest draws into one stadium — a deliberate showcase for the Wanderers, which has long been one of world cricket's most atmospheric grounds. For India, the draw is heavy on spectacle from the start: Australia, then Pakistan, then Afghanistan in the first eight days.

The new Super 7 format is a genuine structural change, scrapping carryover points for a clean second round that keeps more teams alive longer. Combined with the qualifier pipeline — four spots still open — the tournament stays in motion for more than seven weeks, from October 2 to the November 21 final.

Diaspora Angle

The October 1 opening of the official ticket ballot — a free, non-first-come-first-served process running until November 21 — gives diaspora fans in North America, the UK and the Gulf a fair shot at seats for the India–Pakistan game and the final. With entry-level tickets from about USD 9.62, family bundles, and student and pensioner pricing, the ICC is clearly courting traveling supporters alongside local crowds.

What's Next

Attention now turns to the Cricket World Cup Qualifier, which decides the final four group-stage places, and to the Super Series in Windhoek that opens the tournament on October 2, 2027. For India fans, the countdown is already running: October 7 against Australia, October 10 against Pakistan — and, if the draw holds, possibly a rematch deep in the tournament.
